To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the WHO/UNICEF JMP has developed a set of health-based targets and performance specifications to guide the evaluation of household water treatment options.

(1) the WHO guidelines for drinking water quality are not adequate to guide the design of household water treatment systems, and that (2) the WHO guidelines need to be supplemented with health-based targets for microbial risk reduction and microbiological performance standards for the systems.
The health benefits of household water treatment and safe storage are well documented and can be substantial in some settings.

the development of health-based targets for household water treatment options and the development of microbiological performance specifications that can be applied to the evaluation of household water treatment options.

the development and evaluation of household water treatment technologies that can be used to improve the microbiological quality of drinking-water in low-income countries, where the burden of water-related disease is highest.

the evaluation of household water treatment (HWT) technologies, including the development and application of performance specifications for HWT products and the development of health-based targets for the evaluation of HWT technologies.
